If so, is the controller then locked out of using Ghord's effect for the rest of the turn?
answer: It would trigger and do nothing. But the limitation is once per turn, so you could trigger Ghord again during the following battle if you had another sacrifice effect or similar.

question: Lost Guardian's graft ability requires sacrificing a unit as its cost. If its text is copied ('two copies of this graft ability'), does resolving both copies require two separate sacrifices, or only one?
answer: It should be two sacrifices — effectively you copy the whole graft stack (cost and effect) twice.

question: Is there any exception to the rule that spells and abilities can only interact with things in the same region — for example, can an 'any target' spell like All-Consuming Blaze hit an opponent directly even if you have no units in their region?
answer: There are no exceptions to the region rule — it's the most important rule in Algomancy. You need to either attack your opponent or be attacked by them to hit them with All-Consuming Blaze. It's not strictly dependent on having units in a region — for example, if all your attacking units die, you're still considered in that region until Regroup.

question: If a deck empties without cards having been recycled to the bottom along the way (e.g. for physical/sleeving reasons), is shuffling the accumulated recycled cards back into a new deck an acceptable substitute?
answer: Yes, technically that's how it should work — recycling to the bottom of the deck is mostly just a shortcut.

question: If an effect (such as from two copies of a graft ability) requires sacrificing a unit as a cost twice, but you only have one unit to sacrifice, does one copy still resolve, or does the whole thing fizzle?
answer: You would not be able to sacrifice two units in that case, so nothing would be sacrificed (since you can't pay the cost), and the ability would fizzle entirely.

question: If an effect requires sacrificing 2-3 units as its cost but you only have 1 unit, do you sacrifice the 1 you have for a partial effect, or does nothing happen?
answer: Nothing happens — if you can't pay the full cost, the ability fizzles entirely.

question: Do +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters on the same unit cancel each other out?
answer: Yes.

question: Can Tidelurker be placed in a region across from opponents without blocking anything?
answer: Yes — if you decide not to block with Tidelurker, it will be in the region but not blocking, so it will see you take damage and get its bonus (e.g. becoming a 2/2).

question: Does Algomancy check a unit's stats for death during an effect's resolution (e.g. after a mid-resolution stat swap), rather than only at normal state-based-action checks like in MTG?
answer: Algomancy has different rules for this than MTG does — stats are checked for death for units that are interacted with during effect resolutions.

question: Does Piercing deal excess damage to the opponent when blocking an empty column?
answer: Piercing doesn't work when blocking an empty column — it has to hit a unit while blocking to work. By default, units don't attack an empty column, so there's no excess damage in that case, unlike when attacking into an empty column.

question: During combat, when there is Swift interaction, when does a damage trigger get put on the stack — does it open a new priority window during swift damage, or does it wait for the start of the after-swift priority window?
answer: Damage triggers would be put on the stack at the start of the after-swift priority window.

question: If there is a non-swift/non-sluggish unit in combat, when does a Flowstone trigger go on the stack?
answer: The trigger would go on the stack at the start of the "after swift" priority window.

question: If there is no Sluggish unit on the battlefield, does normal combat damage just happen with no extra priority window, meaning you'd need to give a unit Sluggish before regular damage to create a window (e.g. for a double-strike-like effect)?
answer: Correct. 95% of the time you would have to give a unit Sluggish before regular damage to get that window.

question: Are all Graft and Augment cards standalone spells, or are there some that can only be used as mods and not played on their own?
answer: They are all standalone cards; graft and augment are just additional things you can do with them.

question: On a card with an "if you do" clause (sacrifice this unit; if you do, discard a card from the defending player), does "if you do" mean you don't have to sacrifice the unit if you dealt damage?
answer: "If you do" means you have to sacrifice the unit in order to get the discard effect. So if the opponent kills it while the trigger is on the stack, for example, you wouldn't be able to sacrifice it, and so wouldn't discard a card from them.

question: If a unit with a "sacrifice this unit; if you do, discard a card from the defending player" style effect is killed by combat damage, can you still sacrifice it to get the discard effect?
answer: Correct, you can't. Although if the unit gets blocked, you generally wouldn't be able to sacrifice/discard a card from the opponent anyway, since it wouldn't hit the defending player for damage.

question: Given a formation where Amphivore (with Astral Painseeker grafted onto it) has Ancient One behind it in one column, and Astral Tidewraith has Bloodwind Revenant behind it in the adjacent column, against an opponent formation with no flying: do both columns have flying, is the attack trigger only on Astral Tidewraith, and are there 6 combat damage triggers total (draw a card + Bloodwind Revenant trigger)?
answer: 1.) Yes. 2.) Yes. 3.) Yes, but you would get two Bloodwind Revenant triggers since Ancient One is also copying that.

question: When a fireball token is created, does it go on the stack, and do you have to declare its target as soon as it's created?
answer: Fireballs go into play when created, not on the stack. You can play them just like any other battle spell, meaning you can wait for the right time to interact — for example with Megadeath.

question: When resolving Hush Mush against a targeted effect, does the resulting spawn come under Hush Mush's controller's control, or under the control of the negated effect's original controller?
answer: It spawns under the control of the negated effect's controller.

question: If a player is being eliminated but had attacked another region whose combat hasn't resolved yet, are their units in that other region also recycled automatically, and can that recycling trigger effects?
answer: All of their stuff everywhere is recycled automatically and all of their effects are removed. (You are welcome to instead let them finish the turn and die during regroup, if your playgroup prefers that.)

question: 1) Does a "whenever you play a unit" trigger fire on cast or on entering the battlefield, does it trigger on itself, and does it trigger on tokens? 2) If I have the initiative and attack into my opponent's region, can I then cast spells targeting any creature my opponent controls there? 3) When the non-initiative player declares blockers, can they leave some units back that neither block nor counter-attack, and if so what zone are they in?
answer: 1.) Play is like cast in MTG, so it's a cast trigger. It doesn't trigger on itself or on tokens. 2.) Yes — once you've attacked into your opponent's region you can interact with their stuff in that region. 3.) Yes, they stay in the same region, just not participating in combat (like creatures in MTG that don't block, still there but not blocking).

question: Can you use Auric Ascendant's ability to recall Powerforge Synergist, move its counters to the Ascendant, and then replay Powerforge Synergist? And more generally, can you take actions "in response" to things during deployment?
answer: You can definitely do that play with Auric Ascendant and Powerforge Synergist. You just can't do stuff "in response" during deployment — you can't take actions unless the stack is empty.

question: Why can't players take actions or interact (e.g. graft a card in response to a trigger) during deployment?
answer: Deployment will never have player interaction, so there's no need for a priority window there — for example, you can't graft cards onto other cards during deployment in response to their triggers. Think of it as "everything is a sorcery during deployment."

question: If I have multiple effects grafted onto a single cause and one of the effects has a target (e.g. a +1/+1 counter to all your units grafted with a delete-target-unit effect), and that target is removed before the graft resolves, does the whole grafted effect fizzle?
answer: Yes, that is currently how it works. (This is a rule Caleb is considering adjusting.)

question: If I augment Harbinger of Immolation onto a spell token, does the spell token permanently gain a static ability that can keep other spell tokens alive?
answer: Currently spells cannot gain static abilities like that, so the only useful thing you can do is give them attributes.

question: Does Nectar Ridge draw a card from Wisps even when Wispweaver is in play?
answer: Nectar Ridge does draw from Wisps, unless Wispweaver is in play — Wispweaver's static ability causes the Wisps to spawn as 2/2s instead of drawing you a card.

question: Do abilities use the stack? If a unit's ability triggers (e.g. destroy all creatures after combat) and I recall that unit in response, does the ability still resolve?
answer: Yes, abilities use the stack, so you could trigger the ability, recall the unit in response, and the ability would still resolve.

question: On cards like Boreal Wanderer, who does "opponent" refer to?
answer: The opposing player (in that region).

question: If I have a graft ability with a cost (like Linked Extinction) grafted onto another unit, do I have to pay that cost and take the effect when the graft triggers, or can I ignore it and just get the other grafted abilities?
answer: You have to pay the cost.

question: Does an Unaware unit that temporarily buffs another unit or places +1/+1 counters on it interact via damage only, meaning it could kill a Robot that way?
answer: Just go with damage for now — as far as Caleb is aware, that's the only place Unaware currently comes up.

question: If a unit has Structural Collapse grafted onto it and it triggers from a virus targeting it, does the controller get a chance to take other actions (like buffing a different unit to sacrifice instead) before choosing what to sacrifice, once all players have passed priority on the virus?
answer: No — they have to sacrifice the moment the trigger happens, before players even get to pass priority.

question: Can you keep augmenting cards from your bin every time cards die, and what happens to a card's mods when the card dies?
answer: In general yes, but keep in mind if a card that died has any mods on it, that card and all of its mods will be erased (removed from the game). So most of the time mods end up being single use (mods are augmented and grafted cards).

question: If I augment a card out of my hand and it later dies in battle, is it removed from the game rather than going to the bin? Is the same true if I augment out of the bin instead?
answer: Correct, it is removed from the game. Same is true if you augment out of the bin (which is typically where augments are used from).

question: Does front/back row position matter when choosing targets for spells or abilities?
answer: No, front and back row doesn't matter for targeting.

question: What counts as an 'Effect' for rules purposes — does it only refer to units on the board?
answer: An Effect is anything on the stack. For example, Ambush is an effect.

question: When attacking or blocking, can units be placed with empty column gaps between them, and do blockers need to be in the exact same column as the attacker, or just adjacent to the overall formation?
answer: It just needs to be somewhere adjacent to the overall attacking/blocking formation. Basically it works the same way as blockers do.

question: During resource acquisition, can you get prismites instead of shards?
answer: Yes, you can grab prismites this way. If you meant shards, technically you could grab those too, but prismites are strictly better.

question: In what order do battles resolve among multiple players, and in a 1v1 game whose attacks resolve first?
answer: Battles resolve clockwise starting from the initiative player's region. In a 1v1 game, the battle resolves with the initiative player's attacks completely before resolving the non-initiative player's attacks, so the initiative player deals combat damage first.

question: Is stack/priority interaction during battle handled the same way as in Magic: The Gathering?
answer: Basically all stack interaction stuff during battle is the same as MTG. A lot of the other stuff can be different — turn order and regions are what trip up MTG players the most.

question: If the original unit behind an 'echo'/copy effect dies while the copy is still on the stack, does the copy fail to resolve since it copies a now-dead unit?
answer: No, it would still resolve. The copy uses last known information about the original.

question: Do Wisp tokens die at the end of the combat phase regardless of whether they attacked or were in formation?
answer: Wisps die in any region where the end of combat phase happens, regardless of whether they were in formation or attacked. But if nobody attacked into the region the wisps are in, battle is skipped, so there is no 'end of combat' phase there and the wisps wouldn't die.

question: When an effect creates a copy of a card (e.g. with Borrower of Forms), is that copy considered a token or a non-token, and can it be targeted as the 'real' card?
answer: The copy wouldn't be a valid target as if it were the original. There isn't really a way to separate the definition of 'token' from 'nontoken' beyond whether it is an actual, real Algomancy card.

question: In a free-for-all game that narrows down to 2 remaining players, does the game switch to 1v1-style initiative/battle rules (attackers declared, then priority, then counter-attacks/blocks), or does it stay in FFA mode with intent cards?
answer: Officially it switches to the 1v1 rules, but it's up to your group's preference — both are valid ways to play it.

question: Does a spell count as an 'Effect' for the purposes of countering it via a static ability that lets you counter a different effect by sacrificing one of its targets?
answer: Yes, everything on the stack is an effect.

question: After declaring an attacking formation, is there a chance to play battle-speed spells before the opponent declares blockers?
answer: Yes, there's a priority window after attacks are declared but before blocks.

question: Do you choose/select a unit (e.g., for a cost like sacrificing a unit) when the spell goes on the stack, or only when it resolves?
answer: Only targets and things within brackets are selected when something goes on the stack. Everything else is decided on resolution — so, for example, you could make a robot and then sacrifice it.

question: Do +1/+1 or -1/-1 counters affect Unaware units, and what happens if an Unaware creature is placed in the same formation column as a Robot, or blocks a Robot?
answer: Unaware units ignore counters, and they kill Robots in the same formation column as them because they ignore counters. Blocking a Robot with an Unaware creature only kills the Robot when damage is actually dealt, not immediately.

question: If Linked Extinction's graft ability triggers during deployment (e.g. from being grafted onto Engorged Caudex), does it require sacrificing a creature, and are opponents affected by it during deployment?
answer: Linked Extinction will trigger during deployment. Opponents would not be affected by it during deployment.

question: Does The Silent's effect apply to spell tokens in its zone?
answer: Yes.

question: In a multiplayer game, if a player who declared an attack is defeated before the battle in the zone their attackers entered is resolved, do those declared attackers still deal damage?
answer: Officially, no — players die immediately and all their units get erased, so the attack would not happen. Groups are welcome to house-rule assigning death during regroup instead, so the attack would happen, if they prefer that.

question: Can graft or augment be used at battle speed, e.g. via a combat-only spell?
answer: Graft and augment are special actions that, by default, can only be done during deployment, even if the card has haste or battle speed. The only exception is virus cards, which let you apply augments from hand during battle.

question: Are there cards that spawn units directly into formation or battle, and can units be spawned before blocks/counterattacks if you don't have initiative?
answer: Yes, there are cards that specifically spawn units into formation (Ambush is a good example). Also, if you don't have the initiative, you can create or spawn units before blocks/counterattacks.

question: Does Flux Resonator cause spawned robots to enter with double counters?
answer: Not exactly double — it's just X+1, so it happens to double a 1/1 but a 2/2 robot would spawn as a 3/3, not a 4/4.

question: If a spell has both 'battle' speed and graft, can it also be grafted during deployment, including from the bin?
answer: Yes.

question: Is 'Delete' the same as 'Die' for rules purposes?
answer: Yes. There's a glossary on the player aid cards with all the terms and definitions.

question: During the priority window in NIT (non-initiative-player) combat, who has priority — always the IT (initiative) player, or the NIT player who is attacking?
answer: Always the IT player.

question: For a static/passive effect that buffs your allies (like Pernicious Photosynthesis), does it apply only to your current allies at the time, or also to allies you spawn later?
answer: It's just your current allies — similar to how Pernicious Photosynthesis works.

question: Can multiple copies of Maelstrom (or Maelstrom plus Ancient One in formation) be used to get the effective benefit of multiple copies on a single spell?
answer: Yes, you should be able to use multiple Maelstrom/Ancient One for multiple copies.

question: When paying a sacrifice cost that requires sacrificing multiple units (for example, to cast Malevolent Machinations), does the order in which you sacrifice units like Maelstrom Charger and Ancient One matter, and can you still sacrifice a unit as part of the cost after a trigger or spell has already gone on the stack?
answer: Sacrificing units to pay a cost happens within the same game action, so the order between them doesn't matter. However, once a trigger or the spell itself is on the stack, you can no longer sacrifice a unit like Ancient One as part of that action.

question: What can spells and spell units target, and can they target things in an opponent's region?
answer: Spell units, spells and effects in general treat targets the same way. They can target anything in the region of the battle that is currently resolving — so if you're attacking into the opponent's region, you can only target things there, and vice versa. Targets still need to be valid per the effect's requirements (e.g., 'deal 3 damage to target unit' requires a unit, not a player, while 'deal 3 damage to any target' could hit a player).

question: If a unit that a spell is targeting gets sacrificed after the spell targets it, does the spell fizzle?
answer: Yes, if that unit was the only target of the spell.

question: Are spell targets tied to the units themselves rather than their column positions, so that swapping a unit's position within a formation wouldn't let it dodge a 'target creature' spell or ability?
answer: Correct.

question: If a unit with Resonant is augmented with Powerful, attacks (putting its trigger on the stack), and is then sacrificed before the trigger resolves, does the trigger still remember that the unit had Resonant, so that a Resonant trigger would also fire?
answer: The unit would remember having Resonant in that case, so yes, that could happen.

question: Do units in a column that are forced to 'Fight' use the attribute-sharing rules of their column (e.g., Deadly, Tough), and can a spell be cast in the priority window after attacks are declared but before blockers are declared?
answer: Units in a column share attributes in all situations — if one unit has Deadly, they all have Deadly; if one has Tough, they all have Tough (doubling defense), regardless of context. When units 'Fight,' they deal damage equal to their power, and any attributes affecting how they deal damage apply. Yes, you can play spells in the priority window after attacks have been declared but before blockers have been declared.

question: In 2v2 games, does each player have their own region, or is there one shared region per team?
answer: There are two ways to play it. The standard way is each player has their own region and controls their own units. You can also play it more like 'two-headed giant,' which is essentially a 1v1 game but with two players sharing one region — teammates share one region but have their own hands, bins, etc.

question: Do spells formatted with an activated-ability-style colon (e.g., 'remove X counters: deal X damage') count as activated abilities for effects that specifically counter activated abilities?
answer: No — it was a mistake to add the colon formatting to those spells; they don't count as activated abilities.

question: If a unit's ability has the augment symbol and I use that unit as a mod, does the moded unit also gain any attribute written elsewhere on the ability, or only the paragraph with the augment symbol?
answer: Only if the attribute is written directly next to the augment symbol does it apply — otherwise it doesn't transfer. It's not a spell effect; modding just adds the text in that paragraph to the target, nothing more.

question: How does Tempest Wrangler's ability work in FFA (free-for-all) games when all players declare attack intent simultaneously?
answer: It can't stop attacks in FFA, but it can force any remaining units to block.

question: Are effects like Ruinbringer's 'after combat, delete all units' region-specific, and for Rockfall 3 (e.g., on Meteor), can you choose the same 2/2 unit three times?
answer: Everything in the game is region-specific with no exceptions. Rockfall 3 is multiple separate effects, so once you choose a 2/2 it would already be dead — but if you had a unit with 10 defense, you could pick it three times.

question: If a unit that a virus was targeting to mod during combat is removed before the virus resolves, does the virus go to the bin or get erased?
answer: It goes to the bin. Viruses are only usable as mods during battle from hand, so you couldn't then re-apply that virus later in the same battle.

question: Does Alluring stop an opponent's unit from attacking in a free-for-all game, or can it still attack without being redirected?
answer: Alluring can't stop attacks in FFA, but it can force blocks for any remaining units — so it's worse in FFA, but still good for making other units harder to block.

question: When you recall a Graft Pile, what happens to the cards in it?
answer: The top unit goes to your hand, and all mods go to the bin.

question: Does Haboob wipe out Robots because of their Unaware attribute?
answer: Yes.

question: How does Reaping interact with a unit dying from the stat change caused by Invasive Reassignment?
answer: If a unit dies due to the stat change from Invasive Reassignment, you get to draw a card any time you have priority — so during battle or deployment.

question: If Soul Tithe negates an enemy unit that has multiple grafts attached, does it negate all of the grafts, or only one?
answer: Grafts are one big effect, so it negates all of them.

question: Unstable Refactor sets a unit to base 5/0, which would kill it. Can adding other base-stat-changing effects to the pile prevent this, or can only counters/stat buffs save the unit?
answer: Base stats apply in a layer below stat changes, so any stat buff would stop the 5/0 from killing the unit — except specifically something else that sets base stats. You can't save it with other base stat modifiers, but you can save it with counters or stat buffs.

question: If I cast Verdant Vengeance on my opponent's creature, can they cast Woodland Warding to Negate it?
answer: Yes — an effect is anything on the stack (spells, abilities, triggered abilities, battle-speed units, etc.), so it can be negated.

question: Does Unaware ignore Powerful, given that Powerful doesn't literally double the attack stat but instead doubles damage dealt (unlike Tough, which doubles the defense stat)?
answer: Unaware does not ignore Powerful. Powerful doubles damage and has no impact on stats.

question: In a live draft game, what happens if the shared deck runs out of cards entirely (through drawing, Glimpse effects, etc.) and no one can draw anymore?
answer: The game ends, and the highest life total wins.

question: For a unit like Aberrant Populace with a large graft chain assembled, if one entry partway down the chain has a bracket cost, do you have to pay that cost for the entire graft trigger to go off, or just for that entry's contribution?
answer: Currently you have to pay it for the entire trigger to go off. There's a potential rules change being considered where each graft condition could fail separately, but that wouldn't happen until at least the expansion.

question: Is Ambush treated like an ETB trigger (the unit enters play, then chooses targets), or like a spell effect where removing the target in response sends the Ambush card to the bin?
answer: It's treated like a spell effect — if you remove the target in response, the Ambush card goes to the bin.

question: If a column loses Alluring after attackers are declared (e.g., the unit with Alluring is removed or Monke is played), does the previously-targeted unit still have to block that column?
answer: Yes — Alluring is a trigger, so it only does anything when the unit attacks. Losing the attribute afterward doesn't change anything that already happened.

question: When Celestial Fluxmorph is used to mod an opposing unit, whose units get any counters referenced in that mod's text — mine or my opponent's?
answer: Nobody does. Modding something just adds the augment text to it, so it doesn't spawn anything or have the 'trigger' function in its text.

question: Can Minor Kraken trigger its grafted effects by declaring "no target" (i.e. choosing zero targets)?
answer: Yes, up to one could include 0, so you could say no targets and still get Manablub if it was grafted onto the kraken.

question: If a graft has multiple grafted effects and one of them targets something that becomes invalid before it resolves, does that fizzle the whole graft, or just that one effect?
answer: You look at the whole graft as one effect. If it has a single target and that target is removed, then it would all fizzle. In Minor Kraken's case, it has two targeted effects, so if Manablub was removed in response it would still resolve because there's another effect with a target.

question: If Corrupting Blight is played during the after-combat priority window, does its control-changing effect happen at that same after-combat step, or the next one?
answer: The next one. "After combat" is shorthand for "at the beginning of the after combat step," so you want to use Corrupting Blight before combat damage if you want to trigger it that turn cycle.

question: For a symmetric effect like Recall, does the initiative player or the non-initiative player choose which creature to bounce first?
answer: It's the initiative player. In Caleb's constructed video, they did a small sequence break because Caleb already knew what he was going to pick - he's not forbidden from picking first, it's just not usually advantageous to do so.

question: Can a unit like Deathglow Strider that damages the opponent every turn keep triggering just by sitting in your deployment area, without attacking or being attacked?
answer: Only if they attack you or you attack them with it. If they attack you and the strider is in play not blocking, it still damages the opponent. But if neither side attacks the other, the strider isn't in the same region as any opponent and there's no battle phase, so it doesn't trigger.

question: Prismites says "This does not use one of your activations for turn." Does that mean you can pitch two cards on turn 1 for two additional resources that can then be activated?
answer: No, because the Prismites themselves start dormant on turn 1.

question: Does Containment Protocol, which stops activated/triggered effects, also stop a played card like BoF while it's on the stack?
answer: BoF is a played card and therefore is an effect while it's on the stack. An activated/triggered effect is a specific type of effect (one that comes from activated or triggered abilities, not played cards), since "effect" is defined as "a played card, or an activated or triggered ability." Containment Protocol only stops activated or triggered effects, meaning it can stop everything besides played cards on the stack. Effects are like fingers - activated/triggered effect is like saying "your thumb": still a finger, but a subset.

question: For Unstable Singularity, if the only units in the region are your own, do you have to target one of your own units with its delete effect?
answer: Yes, you do - it says "delete target unit" rather than "delete up to one target unit," so a legal target must be chosen even if it's your own.

question: If a card changes controller, does that reset its once-per-turn bounded graft ability so it can trigger again that turn?
answer: No, the once-per-turn restriction is a property of the card, so changing controllers wouldn't affect that.

question: Does a card's ability reset (allowing a once-per-instance trigger to happen again) if it leaves play and comes back, similar to Magic's "new object" rule when a card is bounced and replayed?
answer: Yes, but it's got to actually despawn and then respawn for that to happen.

question: In an FFA game with more than 3 players, can you only attack the players seated directly to your left or right, meaning you can't interact with a player further away until the players between you are eliminated?
answer: In general that is correct - you can't attack players more than just to your left or right. You could interact with a farther player if, for example, you both attacked the same player.

question: If a Wisp token has an "after combat" sacrifice effect but is created after the after-combat step has already passed for that turn, does it still need to be sacrificed that turn?
answer: No, you would've already missed the "after combat" window, so it wouldn't be sacrificed that turn.

question: If a unit has +1/+1 counters and then receives enough -1/-1 counters to kill it, do the plus and minus counters cancel out before the unit dies, like in Magic: The Gathering?
answer: Same as MTG - they cancel out before it dies, but any excess -1/-1 counters would remain, causing it to die.

question: What happens if a player needs to draw a card but their deck is empty?
answer: In constructed, you lose.

question: If I play a card like Spawntender as a unit (rather than using it as a mod) during combat, do I still get its normal card effect (e.g. creating an 8/8 unit)?
answer: Yep! Mods are just additional options for what you can do with the cards, but they all work "normally" when played, not as mods.

question: During the battle phase, can I target a creature that isn't in the region where combat is currently happening with a spell?
answer: No, you can only interact with stuff that's in the region where the current battle is resolving - everything else outside that region effectively doesn't exist. Even for effects like "sacrifice a unit," only what's in that region can be sacrificed.

question: Can Warden be used to redirect a graft effect that has two separate targets, such as Squish and Overbloom, so both target the Warden instead?
answer: Yes, you could make both Squish and Overbloom target the Warden, but you'd have to pay separately for each redirection.

question: Is there such a thing as a +X/+X counter as opposed to a +1/+1 counter, and how do spell tokens work compared to spells played from hand?
answer: There's no such thing as a +X/+X counter - it's all X +1/+1 counters. Counters track permanent changes to a unit; giving a unit +X/+X isn't giving it counters because that stat change is temporary. Spell tokens work essentially the same as spells played from hand - whenever you have priority you can play them, targeting is declared when you play them, and they go on the stack and resolve when all players pass priority.

question: Does a card like Malicious Hardware, which says "whenever one of your units dies, do X," trigger when the unit with that ability itself dies, or only when other units die?
answer: Yes, it triggers when itself dies - otherwise it would say "other."

question: If I have 5 copies of Fireball (a burst spell) and a Voltwrath Behemoth in play, does its trigger fire once or 5 times? Also, if The Silent is in play and I only have 6 untapped resources, am I forced to try to cast all 5 burst Fireballs together, or can I choose to play fewer?
answer: It triggers 5 times - the Fireballs are still individual spells so you get all those triggers. You can decide not to play some of the Fireballs, and the ones you don't play will be erased.

question: In a 3-player FFA game, when the first player is eliminated, what happens to the draft pack they were currently drafting from?
answer: It gets removed from the game.

question: Do spell tokens get erased if no combat happens during a turn?
answer: Yes, they get erased during regroup, and regroup always happens regardless of whether combat does.

question: If a card has a bounded ability on top with an unbounded ability grafted underneath it, does the unbounded part still trigger freely whenever its own condition is met?
answer: No, the top ability of the card limits all of the abilities grafted onto it.

question: Can the unit created by Hooba Lin's formation ability create a new column?
answer: Yes.

question: Three formation questions: 1) If two units in formation share Deadly and each deal 1 damage, does the Deadly damage carry through a whole column of blockers, or does it only kill the front unit? 2) If a blocker ends up in an empty lane during defense, does it just sit there, or does it hit the opponent? 3) Does Piercing (excess damage going through to the player) work regardless of zone and damage source, including for a Piercing unit assigned to an empty lane?
answer: 1) You only need to assign lethal damage to the front unit before it carries to the back, so with Deadly, 1 damage is enough to kill the front unit and another 1 is enough to kill the unit behind it - in general, 2 Deadly damage can take out a whole column. 2) A blocker sitting in an empty lane just sits there doing nothing; blockers don't hit players by default, only attackers do. 3) Piercing works on any source of damage - blocking, attacking, spells, fighting, etc. The only exception is a Piercing unit blocking an empty column, which doesn't hit anything; if it blocks an actual unit, the excess damage hits the player.

question: If I sacrifice a unit to pay the cost of Sacrificial Burst, does a trigger like Rune Channeler's 'when you play a spell' ability still trigger for that sacrificed unit?
answer: I don't believe it triggers if you sac it to pay the cost.

question: If I play Tidal Reversion, can I pay 2 mana to get 2 units off Xenopod Progenitor, since its text says 'one or more' and there are two different players involved?
answer: Yes, you can.

question: Are effects like General Smof's 'After Combat, each player sacrifices a unit' and Bloodwind Revenant's 'you may sacrifice a unit' limited to the region the ability's source is in, rather than applying to all players/units everywhere?
answer: Everything in the game is region specific - mentally add 'in this region' onto every effect. So General Smof's ability means each player in this region sacrifices a unit in this region, and Bloodwind Revenant's ability means you may sacrifice a unit in this region.

question: If a column becomes empty (e.g. its only attacker is removed) before blocks are declared, can it still be blocked?
answer: Empty columns close up before blocks are declared, so there is no column left to block.

question: In a free-for-all game, if my opponent attacks me with a unit and I gain control of it (e.g. via Download) during a priority window before blocks, is it still attacking, does it just sit in my region able to block, or can I use it to attack a different opponent? What about in 1v1 or teams?
answer: You gain control of it, so it's no longer attacking and would be able to block. It can't attack an opponent in the same turn in an FFA game since there's only one declare-attackers step per turn (it could attack them the following turn). In 1v1 or teams, you could use it to attack the same turn if you were the non-initiative player and stole it before the attack step happened.

question: With a bound trigger like Bripp's that can be used once a round, is it usable during any priority window, or only at a specific time? Also, can virus units be played as units (not just as augments) during the battle step?
answer: With Bripp, the effect happens on resolution of the spell, so it doesn't do anything while Bripp is in play (similar to Leaping Lillik). You cannot play viruses as units during the battle step - it only lets you use them as augments. Units that can be played during battle have the battle symbol.

question: If a 4/4 unit has resonant, piercing, powerful, swift, sluggish, and thieving, what's the maximum number of thieving triggers you get? Also, if you deal electric damage to the middle blocker in a row of three, can the damage jump from the middle to the left blocker and then to the right blocker?
answer: The most thieving triggers you can get is 2 (one from swift damage, one from sluggish damage). For electric, you can't jump left and then right - you have to draw a non-intersecting path through the units.

question: When a card like Organics Exchange says units 'switch positions,' does that mean if both units are in formations they swap exact spots in each other's formations? Do effects targeting either unit still apply correctly after they move?
answer: Yes, that's what it means - they switch positions within the formations. Effects target units, not positions, so the effects are unchanged by the units moving around.

question: If a trigger like Mentor's 'when you create a token' is granted by an unbounded graft, but the top-level condition on the card is bounded (e.g. Gardener's once-per-turn 'create a 1/1 unit'), does the whole ability become bounded?
answer: If the top condition is bounded, the whole thing is bounded. So Mentor will only trigger once per turn in that case.

question: 1) Does a fizzled (negated) spell or unit still trigger 'when you play a spell/unit' effects? 2) What are the stats of a column in formation containing Child of Aether (2/0, Balanced) and Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough)?
answer: 1) Yes - those triggers happen when you play the spell, before it resolves, so even if the spell gets negated, the triggers still happen. 2) Balanced always applies last, so the total is 8/8, with Child of Aether at 2/2.

question: How does Maelstrom Charger's ability to copy a spell work without using the stack, if you can't take actions while things are on the stack?
answer: Maelstrom Charger is basically an additional cost to play a spell - you can't take actions while things are on the stack, but this isn't an action, it's an additional cost you can pay when playing a spell that allows it to be copied.

question: Is there a priority window after the initiative player (IT) declares attackers but before the non-initiative player (NIT) declares their attackers, giving the IT a chance to disrupt the NIT's units before their counterattack?
answer: Yes.

question: If a card like Ambush recalls one of your own units that has multiple existing augments on it, do all the existing augments/mods get removed?
answer: When something gets recalled, all its mods go to the bin.

question: Do we check for unit deaths between individual effects within a multi-effect graft, rather than only after the whole graft resolves?
answer: We check for death between effects on any units affected. This is how Flame of History is able to get 'ownership' of kills.

question: Where do erased cards go, where do deleted cards go, and does 'despawn' cover every way a unit can leave the battlefield (dying, erasing, being recalled to hand, etc.)?
answer: Erased cards are removed from the game forever - you'll never interact with them again, so put them in a pile outside the game (like exile in MTG, but more permanent). Deleted cards go to the bin (equivalent to being destroyed/leaving the battlefield in MTG). Yes, despawn means leaving the battlefield (the opposite of spawning), which covers dying, erasing, being recalled to hand, etc.

question: Do combat-based triggers go on the stack before moving into the After Combat step? And if multiple sacrifices happen at the same time, is there a priority window between them?
answer: Combat-based triggers show up on the stack right at the start of After Combat (e.g. 'when I deal combat damage, do X'). Sacrifices are resolved simultaneously, so there's no window between the first and second sacrifice.

question: If Channel Through has you target your own units on cast to deal damage to them, then lets you distribute that damage among an opponent's units, does it still count as targeting the opponent player for effects that care about that?
answer: Channel Through targets the player, so yes, you're good.

question: Does Unaware check printed values rather than current/base values, and does Poisonous still trigger Resonant?
answer: Correct - Unaware checks printed values, not base values. For example, Haboob will kill a +7/+7 1/2 with 4 damage marked on it. Poisonous still triggers Resonant - it would now deal 3, since Resonant triggers off the first loss or gain.

question: If a damage effect targets the front card of a column, does any of that damage carry over to the back card of the column?
answer: You just need to assign enough damage to the front card to kill it before any replacement effects would apply.

question: Do defending units also get organized into a front row and back row, or is that only used for attacking formations?
answer: Yes, defending units also get a front and back row.

question: In a multiplayer game where you have two neighbors on the same side, how do intent cards work for attacking, and does a unit die if its defense becomes zero for any reason?
answer: You can only attack your immediate neighbors. Yes, units with 0 defense die.

question: In constructed decks for the official competitive format, how does the sideboard work - is it 15 different cards that can be added in 1 or 2 copies, or does it need two copies of any card you might want to swap in?
answer: You get 45 total cards to build a deck with: 30 go in the main deck and 15 go in the sideboard, with a maximum of 2 copies of any card across the 45 total. (Sideboards will probably end up smaller than 15 long term.)

question: If you kill a unit in response to its own ability being on the stack, does that ability fizzle, or does it still resolve?
answer: It still goes off unless the ability specifically says otherwise (it would need an 'if' clause, like Hooba-Nan has).

question: If every unit belonging to the target player has died in a region before a spell targeting that region is put on the stack, can the spell still resolve even though the player has nothing left there before Regroup?
answer: Yes - having units in a region doesn't matter. Once you've attacked into a region, you're considered there until Regroup.

question: If Immolate is grafted onto Aberrant Populace, can you sacrifice a wisp that Aberrant Populace spawns within the same effect, or do you have to sacrifice it before the first bracketed effect resolves?
answer: You have to sacrifice it before the first effect, unfortunately, because of the brackets.

question: How does the Virus keyword interact with Augment, and can non-virus augments target opponents' units? Also, for Slink specifically, if you augment an opponent's unit with it, who draws the card?
answer: Virus lets you play that card as an augment even outside deployment (e.g., during combat from hand), and it can also be used as a regular augment during deployment. However, augments can only be put onto your own units, since there's no interaction across regions during deployment, and this restriction applies to viruses used as regular augments too. If you augment Slink onto an opponent's unit, they draw the card - there's no ownership of the effect, so whoever controls the unit controls the Slink trigger. Everything on the stack is treated as an effect, and you can keep activating abilities as long as you have mana for it and the ability isn't otherwise bounded/limited.

question: If a unit augmented with Slink (which is controlled by the opponent since it was augmented onto their unit) gets recalled to hand, does the Slink card go to the opponent's bin or to the augmenting player's bin?
answer: Correct - it goes to the opponent's (the controller's) bin, not the augmenting player's.

question: What happens to Cache cards if they aren't played that turn - are they discarded, put on the bottom of the deck, or something else?
answer: They stay in the cache, which in the base game is functionally equivalent to being erased.

question: In a free-for-all game, if a player is eliminated during their own combat, does their board still deal combat damage to other players during those other players' combats later in the round?
answer: According to the official rules, no. (Caleb personally house-rules it so that players all live until regroup, but that's not the official rule.)

question: Are the defending player's units in formation before or after the priority window that occurs following attack declaration?
answer: Units of the defending player aren't in formation until after there is a priority window. The order is: attacks are declared, then a priority window, then blocks.

question: What are the basic setup rules for constructed play?
answer: Decks are 30 cards, with a maximum of 2 copies of any card. (Caleb also advises playing more interaction than you'd expect to want, since one-ofs/situational cards can be great in this game.)

question: Can Bloodwind Revenant's sacrifice-a-creature trigger be used to sacrifice a creature that would otherwise die to a Sluggish blocker, before the Sluggish damage is dealt?
answer: Yes, that's possible - Sluggish damage happens afterwards.

question: If a spell creates units before attacks/blocks are declared, can those new units be assigned as attackers or blockers? Also, when declaring attackers and moving into an opponent's region, what are legal targets for spells cast in that region?
answer: Newly created units can be assigned as attackers or blockers, but only via a haste spell, or if you're the defending player, since there's no priority window before attacks during battle. As for targeting: anything in the region is a valid target. If you're the only one who has attacked, that includes all of your opponent's units, your opponent themselves, and any of your own units that attacked - but your own units that didn't attack can't be targeted during that battle in your opponent's region.

question: In 2v2 games with different regions, can a teammate send blockers or cast spells to help defend a player being attacked in that player's own region?
answer: No, they cannot send blockers to help defend, and consequently they can't use spells to help defend a player either (at least within that player's region). They can use spells to help attack, though - for example, if a teammate has the initiative and attacks, both teammates could use spells to help whittle down a massive enemy army during that attack.

question: In 2v2 games with shared regions, since you share a region with your teammate during your deployment phase, can you augment or modify your teammate's units during your deployment phase?
answer: Yes.

question: If Ruinbringer dies during the combat damage step, does its ability still trigger after combat?
answer: No.

question: In a 1v1 game, if the opponent attacks you, can you target them with a spell like a fireball, even though you're not counterattacking?
answer: Yes - any player in the region is a valid target.

question: If you sacrifice Ravenous Fireslinger as a cost to pay for a spell, does its own "whenever a spell is played" trigger fire off of that spell?
answer: No - the sacrifice cost happens before the spell is considered played, so there's no trigger. (Note: there are 'stolen cards' effects that can replace a card when it goes to your hand or deck.)

question: For Galactic Germination, does its formation-based effect count ALL attacking or blocking units a player controls in that region, or only a specific column?
answer: It's all attacking or blocking units they control in that region.

question: If the player with the initiative makes an all-out attack and the defending player chooses not to block but instead makes an all-out counterattack, and both attacks would be lethal to each other, who wins - is it a draw, or does the initiative-taking player win?
answer: The initiative-taking (IT) player wins. Their attack damage is resolved first, since that battle is finished completely before the counterattack's damage resolves.

question: Can a unit have both Graft and Augment on it at the same time, and how do the two interact?
answer: Graft and Augment don't interact with each other. A unit can have both, but they do different things: Graft only adds what's after the graft symbol onto the trigger condition of the top card, while Augment adds a complete ability from another card.

question: If a unit is forced to block via an Allure-style effect but cannot block a particular column because it has Evasive, can it instead be used to block a different column?
answer: Yes.

question: For an effect like Flamebreath Initiate that lets you change a spell's target, do all possible targets need to be declared at the time of casting, or can you redirect to a target not originally declared?
answer: You're not adding new targets - you're just changing existing (already-declared) targets.

question: Can Haste spells be played during the deployment phase?
answer: Yes, they can.

question: During a battle, can a spell or effect target two units that are in different regions - for example, an attacker from the initiative-taking player's region and a counterattacker in the non-initiative player's region?
answer: No. Units in regions outside of the region you're currently interacting in are treated as if they don't exist. Units leave the region when they're sent for counterattacks.

question: Is Piercing functionally different from Trample, in that Piercing works in more scenarios such as while blocking or during fight tricks?
answer: Yeah, pretty much.

question: When Rousing Spirit triggers and puts a unit into formation behind it, does that unit enter as 'attacking' or simply 'in formation'?
answer: These are the same thing.

question: If you're the defending player and create fireball-type spell tokens in your own zone during defense, can you target those spell tokens at the attacking opponent's face, even though the opponent isn't in your zone?
answer: As long as your opponent has attacked (entering your zone), they're in the zone, so you can target them.

question: If the initiating team (IT) declares an attack into a non-initiating team's (NIT) region, whose priority does the following priority window start with?
answer: IT (the initiating team) always gets priority first.

question: Does Mischievous Reclaimer's death trigger fire if it is the one that dies, and in what order is combat damage applied to multiple units?
answer: Combat damage all happens at the same time. Mischievous Reclaimer will still trigger from its own death, since it counts as an ally dying.

question: Does Stellarspore Harvester's "after combat" trigger fire once per region's after-combat step, or for the whole combat phase?
answer: It only triggers in the after-combat step in its own region. Everything in the game only affects its own region — you can mentally add "in this region" to every line of card text.

question: If a unit's life total drops to 0 or below while there are still other effects on the stack, does it die immediately or only after all the stacked effects finish resolving?
answer: It dies immediately — death checks work basically the same as in MTG.

question: When assigning combat damage to a chump blocker like Trashling, is there a minimum amount of damage that must be assigned to it before the rest can be assigned to units behind it?
answer: You need to assign at least 2 damage to Trashling (enough to be lethal to it); you can put the rest behind it.

question: If a Graft trigger has multiple clauses, some of which target, and all of those targets become illegal/are removed, is the entire ability countered?
answer: Yes.

question: Slink gives other units in its formation row Thievery. If that whole column goes unblocked and deals damage equal to its total power to the defending player as a single source, how many times does Thievery trigger?
answer: You draw one card — the column deals its damage as a single source, so the triggered ability only happens once.

question: Does a unit that "spawns with X counters" count as having had counters "put on" it, for effects that trigger off putting one or more counters on an ally?
answer: Yes.

question: Do most triggered or activated abilities of a unit continue to resolve normally even if the unit that generated them dies before they resolve? And do such abilities already on the stack ignore a later effect like Monke entering play?
answer: Both correct.

question: Are spell units best understood as an effect that, if it resolves, creates a unit — without that creation itself using the stack?
answer: Yep, that's exactly how they work.

question: If a player is attacked by multiple attacking parties at once, do they form separate defending formations for each attack?
answer: Yes, defending formations are separate, but everything is still in the same region.

question: If Recyclable Sentinel's effect comes before Linked Extinction within the same Graft trigger, can the sacrifice required by Linked Extinction be paid using the token from Recyclable Sentinel, or must the sacrifice happen when the Graft trigger is put on the stack?
answer: Linked Extinction requires sacrifice as an additional cost (that's what the brackets mean), so you have to sacrifice to it first.

question: When placing a unit into an empty blocking position after blockers have already been declared (e.g. via Hooba-Pon's ability), and some positions have altered conditions like Evasive, Sneaky, or Flying that apply at the declare-blockers step, can the unit be placed in any empty position, or only in a position that would have been a legal block at the time blockers were declared?
answer: You're correct — you can only place it somewhere that would have been a legal block at the time (of declaring blockers).

question: On the small player reference cards next to the draft zones, what does a number in parentheses like "(1)" next to an ability icon mean, versus having no number?
answer: Those little player cards next to the draft zones have some info on them. The (1) indicates that ability can only trigger once per turn; without the 1, it means it can happen as many times as you want.

question: For Arc Lightning, can excess electric damage chain to more than one adjacent unit, or only to a single adjacent unit?
answer: It's a recursive definition. Any excess damage after hitting the first unit is still electric damage, so it can be redirected again. You basically get to draw a non-overlapping path through the formation until you run out of electric damage.

question: If a spell has multiple targets (for example Forced Germination, which puts -1/-1 counters on one target unit and +1/+1 counters on another) and one of the targets becomes invalid before it resolves, does the spell still resolve using the remaining valid target?
answer: Yes, as long as the spell still has a valid target, it will resolve.

question: Ghord makes each opponent sacrifice a nontoken unit whenever you sacrifice a unit. If an opponent has no creature in the region Ghord is in, do they still need to sacrifice one?
answer: No, because they can't.

question: Does a spell need a valid target in order to resolve? For example, can a spell with a search/find effect that finds nothing (like Delver of Mysteries), or a spell with no target requirement at all (like Accelerated Germination), still resolve?
answer: There's a set of rules for what spells need in order to resolve. Mostly it comes down to whether they have a targeted effect: if they do, they need at least one valid target to resolve. Otherwise, they can resolve without issue. For example, a spell like Accelerated Germination (which just creates a unit, with no target needed) can resolve fine even with no valid targets.

question: Spewing Mushroom creates a poison unit when it enters formation. (1) Can that poison unit be created before I have a chance to move my units to another region to avoid it? (2) Do "whenever you play a spell" triggers fire when a spell unit is played? (3) What happens if a spell unit gets negated?
answer: The poison can be cast before the units can run away from it — there is a priority window after attacks are declared, before blocks/counterattacks happen. Yes, playing a spell unit triggers spell-cast effects, and then the unit is played as a card. Negating a spell unit will negate the whole thing (the unit goes to the discard).

question: Does Bellowing Boulder's enter-formation ability damage itself? Also, if it has deadly and is attacking with initiative, is there a way to answer it before it repeatedly deals damage to the whole region every turn?
answer: It does damage itself. That's a spicy combo — we haven't had any problems with it so far, but I'll make a note of it. In that case, you could either erase your own combo in the process (if it was augmented), or the opponent could simply remove the deadly-granting unit from the formation to take deadly away from the boulder.

question: What does the Deadly keyword mean in terms of how much damage is needed to kill a unit?
answer: Deadly means any damage is lethal — dealing even 1 damage from a deadly source is enough to kill a unit.

question: If an attacker with deadly is double-blocked (two units stacked in the same slot), does the second unit in line also die from the deadly damage?
answer: Yes. Two instances of deadly damage are dealt: the first kills the front unit, and the second kills the unit behind it (e.g. Rotspore Herald).

question: Can a player choose X = 0 when paying an X cost for an ability or spell?
answer: Yes, X can be chosen as 0. Caleb noted he was still working to make everything function correctly with X costs of 0 (referencing Frosted Denial as an example).

question: If a Spell Unit's spell effect (like Leaping Lillik's '(1) Delete target unit') is negated or fizzles because it loses its target, does the unit still spawn onto the battlefield afterward? Also, what's the difference between 'Negate target spell effect' and 'Negate target non-spell effect'?
answer: If the spell effect loses its target or fizzles, the unit will NOT spawn afterward. 'Effect' means anything on the stack, so 'Negate target effect' is like 'negate target spell, activated ability, or triggered ability' in Magic. 'Negate target spell effect' will counter anything with the spell type, which is most of the interaction, but also units like Leaping Lillik (since it's a Spell Unit). 'Negate target non-spell effect' covers most everything else, like activated and triggered abilities. There isn't much need to negate units themselves, so that hasn't been given its own specific wording yet, since only a few units can be negated.

question: Channeled Boon lets you divide its +4/+4-until-regroup effect between the target unit and adjacent units. What happens if the target unit has no adjacent units?
answer: It would just give the target unit +4/+4 if it has no adjacent units.

question: For keywords like Fight (and Bite), is the damage dealt equal to the unit's total effective power?
answer: Yes, that's how Fight is worded too — it's just damage equal to the unit's power.

question: Do Blessed units gain life at the exact same time they deal damage, or does the life gain happen as a separate triggered ability that goes on the stack?
answer: Simultaneous. (Note: Parasitic Parishioner itself isn't Blessed — only the 'Whenever you gain life, each opponent loses that much life' effect it can grant is augmentable.)

question: Rot Jelly replaces a column's combat damage to players with 1 rot instead of normal life loss. If a Lethal unit (like Gublin) is in that column, is the combat damage still considered to have been applied, so that Lethal still triggers?
answer: Yes.

question: Spellbind's Wisp tokens have 'Sacrifice me after combat.' Can I use one of these Wisps to pay the cost of Spellbind's other mod, '[Sacrifice a unit]: I deal 4 damage to any target,' since the Wisp is going to be sacrificed after combat anyway?
answer: No.

question: In team games, does an individual player still have their own initiative even though the rulebook only describes the team as a whole having initiative? What order do multiple regions resolve in during a team game?
answer: Yes, individual players still have initiative within the team-based system (the pinned rulebook was outdated; see the current manual at calebgannon.com). In team games you resolve the non-initiative team's regions clockwise first, then the initiative team's regions clockwise.

question: Can a unit enter an enemy region during the Attack step without being placed into formation, so it can't easily be blocked and killed?
answer: No, currently you have to attack (i.e. be placed into formation) to send a unit or other card into an enemy region. This is a rule Caleb is open to changing in the future.

question: If overkill damage kills Lithoghul or Restitution (both have 'Whenever I am dealt damage, I deal that much damage back'), does their damage-reflection ability still trigger?
answer: Yes, they trigger even off overkill (lethal) damage, e.g. dealing 5 damage to a 4-defense unit still triggers its 'whenever I am dealt damage' ability, even though the unit dies before it can use that damage to save itself.

question: If Mohruung is targeted by Squish, does Mohruung's 'when I become targeted, create a Crystal 2' trigger before Squish resolves, and can the resulting Crystal buff increase the damage dealt by Squish? Also, is Squish's damage amount fixed at cast time or recalculated on resolution?
answer: Yes, that all works as expected. Triggered abilities and buffs (like the Crystal from Mohruung) can go on the stack above Squish and resolve before it, increasing Mohruung's defense used for Squish's damage. In general, things are checked on resolution, not when the spell/ability was cast, unless being in a particular state is itself a requirement for a condition to trigger.

question: During the battle phase, when exactly can players play spells/interact (including battle spells and during formation setup), and does deployment happen simultaneously for both players?
answer: You can play cards during any of the specifically marked priority windows in the turn structure. In 1v1: Planning (refresh resources, draw 2, draft, gather/activate resources, play mods from hand) is followed by Battle, split into two phases. Phase 1: the initiating team attacks into the non-initiating team's regions, priority window, non-initiating team declares blocks (and may send their own units to counter-attack), priority window, combat damage, priority window. Phase 2 mirrors this with the non-initiating team attacking into the initiating team's regions. Then Regroup (return units to your region, reset damage/buffs, erase spell tokens), then Deployment (play cards/mods from hand or bin, then end turn). If you play Magic: the Gathering, the interaction timing windows during battle are essentially the same as in that game.

question: Do declaring blockers and sending your own units to attack (formation lock) happen at the same moment? For example, would Bellowing Boulder (deals 1 damage to each unit when it attacks or blocks) NOT damage units that are being sent into the enemy region on that same step?
answer: Correct, that's also correct. You don't need to fix (lock in) your formation until you move to that attack step, so declaring blocks and sending attacking units effectively happen together at that point, meaning a unit like Bellowing Boulder blocking wouldn't damage units that are simultaneously being sent out to attack.

question: While attacking in another player's region, is your hand considered to be 'in' that region and therefore interactable, the same way your bin, resources, and you as a player are?
answer: Yes, your hand is considered to be in the region when you attack in another player's region, making it interactable there, per the general rule that once a player has entered a region, their bin, hand, resources, and the player themself can all be interacted with.

question: If an opponent's Tidal Reversion targets my unit to recall it, but I respond by Ambushing in Mirrorback Ambusher to take that unit's place (removing the original target), does Tidal Reversion fail to recall the opponent's own unit since one of its targets is gone?
answer: No, Recall (Tidal Reversion) will still recall the opponent's own unit. Effects do their best to resolve: as long as at least one legal target remains, the effect still resolves for that target. The exception is anything that performs an 'exchange', which requires both original targets to remain valid in order to take place.

question: For units with 'I <do something>' triggered or activated abilities (e.g. Throwing Boulder's 'Sacrifice me: I deal 3 damage...'), must the unit still be in play when the ability resolves off the stack?
answer: No, the unit doesn't need to still be in play for the ability to resolve. Throwing Boulder, for example, wouldn't function at all if it had to still be in play to deal its damage, since it sacrifices itself as part of the cost. In general, once an ability has triggered or been activated and is already on the stack, it resolves without requiring its source to still be in play.

question: Does damage dealt by a Poisonous unit (in the form of -1/-1 counters) count as 'damage' for triggers like 'whenever I am dealt damage'?
answer: Yes, Poisonous damage counts as damage. It is not a replacement effect; if it were, the card would say 'if a poisonous unit would deal damage, instead put that many -1/-1 counters on the opposing unit.' Instead it says the unit 'deals damage in the form of -1/-1 counters,' meaning it is still damage, just represented as counters.

question: For modal cards like Wither and Bloom (choose to put a -1/-1 counter on each enemy OR a +1/+1 counter on each of your units), is the mode chosen as part of paying the cost, or as part of resolving the effect?
answer: Choosing the mode is the cost, not the effect itself — you decide whether you're putting counters on your stuff or the enemy's stuff as you play the spell. Then when the effect resolves, the chosen mode happens.

question: Are region-specific triggers (like Wandering Blightshell's "when you put a counter on an enemy") only active for things happening in that unit's own region, and do units need to block or participate in combat to trigger "after combat" effects?
answer:
Everything in the game is region specific. So nothing will ever impact anything in another region. You should be able to completely ignore cards in other regions when resolving a battle.

Units don't need to block to trigger (unless the card specifically says so). Just being in the region is enough.

If a card says after combat it doesn't need to attack or block to get the effect, but a battle does need to take place in that region for "after combat" to trigger. So if the unit is in a region where nobody is attacked, it will not trigger. In general, after combat is the hardest trigger to make happen.

question: Can Woodland Warding (negate all enemy effects targeting allied effects, players, or units) negate a spell that doesn't target anything specifically, like Haboob?
answer: It cannot — that's the downside of Woodland Warding's interaction, since it only negates effects that target something allied. Hush Mush, which negates an effect directly rather than needing it to target something, is really the only wood counter spell that could stop Haboob.

question: Auric Ascendant's ability lets you recall another ally to gain flying and +2/+0 until regroup. Can this be activated during deployment, and if so, how long does the flying last?
answer: You can also activate it during deployment, and if you do, the flying will last until the end of the following combat (not just the current one).

question: If I'm being attacked by a 1/1 unit and I block with a 7/7 unit that has Piercing (e.g. from Pernicious Photosynthesis), does the 6 excess damage get dealt to the attacker's controller?
answer: Yes.

question: For Infernal Cultivator's ability (1x, Sacrifice X units: Create X Fireball 1 units), when can it be activated, how long do the Fireball 1 tokens last, and what does the "1x" restriction mean?
answer: It's an activated ability, so you can do it any time you have priority (during battle or deployment). The fireballs will stay until regroup, yes. The 1x also means you can only use this once per turn.

question: If a 13/4 attacker with Piercing is blocked by a 1/1 Hooba-Lin, and before combat damage the non-active player casts Phytochemical Protection on Hooba-Lin, how is the combat damage split between the blocker and the piercing damage to the player?
answer: At least 1 damage must be assigned to Hooba-Lin (the attacker could assign more if they wanted to); the rest is dealt to the defending player as piercing damage.

question: If a source has Powerful, a Conduit-style 'noncombat damage plus 1' effect, and Resonant, and it would deal 1 damage to an enemy unit, how does the damage math and triggering actually work, including whether the Resonant damage to the player also gets boosted again?
answer: The damage first gets +1 from the Conduit-style effect, then is doubled by Powerful, so 1 damage becomes (1+1)*2 = 4 damage to the unit. Resonant then triggers to deal that same 4 damage to the unit's controller, but that instance of damage also gets +1 and is doubled again by Powerful.

question: Can Gravitational Correction be used to change the target of my own effect (e.g. redirecting Vaporweave Eidolon's 'create a copy of target token' ability from a token that just died to a different token I still control) in order to prevent the effect from fizzling?
answer: Yes.

question: If Meteor Shower creates multiple copies of the burst spell Rockfall and each copy hits something, does Ember of Life's 'create that many 1/1 units when a spell effect deals damage' trigger treat all the Rockfall damage as one combined source, or once per copy?
answer: Each copy of Rockfall is a separate source, so Ember of Life triggers separately for each copy rather than combining them into one bigger trigger.

question: If Amphivore is grafted onto another unit (for example Astral Painseeker) and its graft condition triggers (three copies of its graft ability as one trigger), how many cards do I draw, and does a graft ability like Lost Guardian's do anything if it's grafted into something else instead of its normal host?
answer: You draw three cards. Lost Guardian doesn't do anything when it's grafted into other stuff.

question: If a unit's stats are changed (e.g. by stacking Aetherflux Golem's augment +2/+2 with Reality Bender's Inverted augment, which inverts stat changes) so that its defense would be reduced to 0, does the unit die immediately, or does an opponent need to use a priority window to reorder the augments first?
answer: It dies. Attribute-based effects (like dying at 0 or less defense) are checked after stat changes have already applied, so the death happens as a result of the final stats rather than requiring the opponent to manipulate the order in a priority window.

question: Does Hexbane Shiitake's ability (exchange control of me for another player's spell) only let you swap with the first spell someone plays, or can you use it once per turn on any qualifying spell?
answer: It can only be chosen to swap once per turn. The wording on the card may need improvement to make this clearer.

question: For Volatile Toxicity, is the sacrifice a unit cost that can be disrupted (e.g. by killing the target of the sacrifice before it happens) since it's paid as part of playing the spell?
answer: The sacrifice is part of the cost, so you can't disrupt the sacrifice itself — by the time anyone gets priority, the sacrificed unit is already dead. You can, however, disrupt the spell/card itself after the sacrifice has happened. That's effectively the difference between a card like Volatile Toxicity and a card like Fight.

question: If a region is not attacked during Phase 1, do both players still get a priority window to cast battle spells in that region?
answer: Phase 1 does not get a priority window if IT did not attack — in regions that are not attacked, you skip battle in that region completely.

question: If Fungal Gardener dies in the same battle as several nontoken enemy units die simultaneously, does its 'whenever a nontoken enemy dies' trigger fire once per enemy that died, even though Fungal Gardener itself died at the same time?
answer: Units see themselves die and would trigger. If Fungal Gardener and three nontoken enemies died at the same time, you would make three 1/1 units. (An opponent is an enemy player.)

question: In Algomancy Cube Draft, what counts as your final hand/deck — just the last two cards you drew, or everything accumulated through the draft?
answer: The hand is your deck, essentially — you'll end with 30 cards in your "hand".

question: Can any Augment card be grafted onto any unit, and when can a Poison spell token (created by an effect) be played during the battle phase?
answer: You are only able to graft cards onto other cards that have a graft symbol — so Bio Toxicity can't be grafted onto Jollyglop. Poison is just a spell token, so if you're able to create one, you could play it whenever you wanted within the battle phase; that would then cause the next effect to trigger. A comparable situation that is possible would be Stoneborn Progenitor.

question: When a graft ability that requires sacrificing a unit is triggered twice (e.g. combined into one 'after combat' trigger), is sacrificing a unit for each instance a required step, or an optional cost you can decline?
answer: Yes, it is required — at least in the current rules, though this is something Caleb is considering changing.

question: Can Unmake (which deletes a target unit with base power 2 or less) target a unit whose printed power is low but whose effective power is boosted to higher than 2 by an ability like Balanced (e.g. Decay Distributor, printed 0/7, made Balanced so its effective stats become 7/7)?
answer: Yep! Base refers to base stats, which is usually the printed stats, unless something specifically modifies the base stats (it would say "becomes base something").

question: If I play Hooba-Lin and Flamebreath Initiate into the same formation at the same time (e.g. Hooba-Lin's ability spawns a unit alongside Flamebreath Initiate), do their triggered abilities have a fixed resolution order or can I choose?
answer: You can choose what order they take place in, so you could put a Hooba-Lin behind your Flamebreath Initiate to get extra firebreathing (an extra adjacent ally boosting the Fireball size).

question: Rider of the Tides triggers when a card enters a player's hand during battle (e.g. recalling a token unit). Does recalling a spell-token also trigger it?
answer: Yes, recalling spell-tokens should also trigger Rider of the Tides.

question: Can X ever be 0 for X-value spells and tokens (like Fireball X or Robot X)?
answer: Yes, X can be 0 for spells and tokens in general now. Caleb is keeping an eye on it and would prefer it not be possible in some specific cases, but rather than make a blanket rule against it, he adds "X can't be 0" text directly on the individual cards where it would be problematic (for example, Instrument of Reassignment's Robot X ability specifies X can't be 0).

question: If an ability lets me play a unit (like Hooba-Pon's "play a unit from your hand into an open position") and I choose to play a spell unit (like Leaping Lillik), does it go on the stack and resolve with normal targeting like any other played spell, or is it played outside the stack in a special way?
answer: It works like a spell on the stack.

question: When a card's text refers to "units they interact with," does blocking count as interacting?
answer: It's essentially "damaging and being dealt damage by," so yes, blocking counts as interacting.

question: Does an ability's "if you do" clause count as its own triggered ability/effect, for example for the purpose of Crevice Lurker (which increases the cost of effects)?
answer: "If you do" in this case doesn't create a trigger, so it's fully confirmed that it doesn't get hit by Crevice Lurker.

question: For Flame Shield's "negate all effects": does "effect" include things like unit abilities and mods, does it only affect cards currently on the stack, and can Flame Shield itself be countered by something else on the stack?
answer: An effect is a played card, or an activated/triggered ability - basically anything that goes on the stack. So "negate all effects" stops anything on the stack below it (anything above it would already resolve first). Yes, it can be countered - since it's an effect, any "negate target effect" would negate it.

question: Does Awoken Tomb need to survive the damage it's dealt for its 'create an X/X unit' trigger to happen?
answer: No, Awoken Tomb's ability triggers just from being dealt damage; it doesn't need to survive. Only cards that specifically say 'survive damage' (like Molten Tormentor, which says 'Whenever I survive damage...') require that condition.

question: Does the Unaware keyword ignore Powerful, Tough, and Inverted, in addition to ignoring counters and temporary bonuses?
answer: Unaware does not ignore Powerful. It does ignore Tough and Inverted.

question: If I control Borrower of Forms copying an opponent's unit (e.g. Good Whale), and the opponent casts Recall targeting that copied unit, can Recall also target Borrower of Forms itself? And if the copied unit leaves play before Borrower of Forms resolves, does Borrower of Forms as a whole fizzle, or just its copy effect?
